Parent: She gets exhausted more easily than her contemporaries. After playing for about an hour, she needs to rest for longer periods compared to other kids her age. This has been observed both at home and during physical activities at school.

Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: Unfortunately, yes. She experiences epileptic seizures. They're not very frequent, but they do occur. We work closely with her neurologist to manage this condition effectively.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding, stomach, bowel).
Parent: In infancy, feeding was a significant challenge. She had trouble latching and would often spit up. However, as she grew older, these issues resolved themselves.

Parent: Developmentally, she seems to lag behind her peers. These aspects worry us, and we hope to address them through physiotherapy and occupational therapy.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: None noted.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A.

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 15% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes. A few require surgery, while others only need monitoring. [Reference Guidelines].

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome commonly have feeding difficulties and swallowing problems. These can lead to aspiration pneumonia, where food enters the lungs through the nose or mouth and travels down the airway. Aspiration pneumonia can be dangerous and requires treatment. [Reference Guidelines].

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more susceptible to developing autoimmune diseases later in life. Research suggests that approximately 10-20% of people with KBG syndrome develop autoimmune conditions such as Type 1 diabetes, lupus, rheumatoid arthritis, and thyroid disease. [Reference Guidelines].

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: She experiences epileptic seizures, which are not frequent but do occur. Management involves close collaboration with a neurologist. [Reference Guidelines].
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Approximately 15% of people with KBG syndrome develop autoimmune conditions, including Type 1 diabetes, lupus, rheumatoid arthritis, and thyroid disease. [Reference Guidelines].

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Babies with KBG syndrome commonly have feeding difficulties and swallowing problems. These can lead to aspiration pneumonia, where food enters the lungs through the nose or mouth and travels down the airway. Aspiration pneumonia can be dangerous and requires treatment. [Reference Guidelines].

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: She struggles to hear whispers and distant voices, and selective hearing can be noticeable. Vision screening is recommended following diagnosis. [Reference Guidelines].
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more susceptible to developing autoimmune diseases later in life. Research suggests that approximately 10-20% of people with KBG syndrome develop autoimmune conditions such as Type 1 diabetes, lupus, rheumatoid arthritis, and thyroid disease. [Reference Guidelines].

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A.

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: Her front teeth are notably larger than those of her peers. Orthodontic assessment is planned following diagnosis. [Reference Guidelines].
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome commonly have feeding difficulties and swallowing problems. These can lead to aspiration pneumonia, where food enters the lungs through the nose or mouth and travels down the airway. Aspiration pneumonia can be dangerous and requires treatment. [Reference Guidelines].

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: She shows developmental delays in various areas, including crawling, walking, playing with toys, using cutlery, using zips and buttons, and toilet training. Current level of education attainment is below average expectations. [Reference Guidelines].
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Most children with KBG syndrome require additional educational support, such as an Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP). Their cognitive abilities fall within the average to gifted range. [Reference Guidelines].

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: She exhibits behavioral differences, such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), anxiety, and sensory integration dysfunction. [Reference Guidelines].
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Behavioral differences are common in KBG syndrome, affecting mood, behavior, and social interactions. Sensory integration dysfunction can impact sleep patterns, digestion, and temperature regulation. [Reference Guidelines].

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: She has brachydactyly (short fingers) with a curvature of the 5th finger (clinodactyly) and an unusual structure of her spinal bones, which can cause an increase in the curvature of the spine (scoliosis). [Reference Guidelines].
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A study of 40 European patients found that 15/40 (38%) had heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes. A small percentage experienced tethered cord, leading to pain and weakness in the legs, urinary and bowel issues, sacral dimple, and asymmetrical gait. [Reference Guidelines].

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Regular dental check-ups.
b) Regular hearing screenings to age 5.
c) Eyesight (ophthalmology) review.
d) Check position of testes in boys.
e) Consider a palate review (particularly if there are feeding difficulties or speech concerns).
f) Consider a cardiac review (including echo and ECG) following diagnosis.
g) Monitor growth velocity: if height is below the 2nd centile consider referral for endocrine investigations on an individual basis and within context of familial heights.
h) Consider review and investigation for tethered cord (MRI) where clinical concerns arise on an individual basis (especially if sacral dimple is present).

This completes the clinical report following the specified 13-category schema layout.

## 2) CARDIOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Around 15% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes. Monitoring is crucial, especially for those with structural abnormalities or previous heart-related issues.

How this affects the patient: N/A
How this affects others with the syndrome: Heart conditions can vary in severity and impact on daily activities, requiring ongoing medical supervision and potential interventions such as echocardiograms, ECGs, and surgical procedures depending on the specific condition.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome commonly experience feeding difficulties, texture preferences, and swallowing issues. These can lead to prolonged hospitalizations for tube feedings and surgeries to correct anatomical issues.

How this affects the patient: N/A
How this affects others with the syndrome: Specific dietary restrictions, nutritional deficiencies, and challenges with food textures and consistency can significantly impact a child's nutrition and overall health. Addressing feeding difficulties requires a multidisciplinary approach involving speech therapists, dieticians, and pediatricians experienced in managing KBG syndrome.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Individuals with KBG syndrome are more susceptible to developing autoimmune diseases and infections. Vaccinations should be administered according to standard protocols, and close observation is essential post-vaccination.

How this affects the patient: N/A
How this affects others with the syndrome: An increased risk of autoimmune reactions and heightened susceptibility to infectious agents necessitates meticulous immunization schedules and vigilant monitoring for adverse effects.

## 5) NEUROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Neurological features can include developmental delays, behavioral differences, seizures, sensorineural hearing loss, cerebellar features (such as weak finger-to-facial grasp reflex and kyphoscolosis), and brain malformations. Management includes physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapies.

How this affects the patient: N/A
How this affects others with the syndrome: Neurodevelopmental outcomes can vary widely, affecting areas such as cognitive abilities, motor skills, sensory processing, and social interaction. Regular neurology evaluations and adaptive physical activity programs tailored to the patient's capabilities are critical components of care.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- KBG syndrome is characterized by conductive hearing loss, which can result from various factors including adenotonsillar hypertrophy, nasal congestion, and subtle anatomical variations. Management involves ENT consultations, sinus treatments, and possible tonsillectomy.

How this affects the patient: N/A
How this affects others with the syndrome: Conductive hearing loss can significantly impair audibility and contribute to speech delay and difficulty with noisy environments. Ongoing ENT assessments and treatment plans are vital for optimizing auditory function.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION

a) How this affects the patient:

## 1) RESPIRATORY

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 15% of patients (38 out of 40) were found to have heart conditions such as changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural abnormalities. A few required surgery, while others required monitoring. N/A.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome may have feeding difficulties, swallowing problems, gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), and vitamin deficiencies due to poor absorption. N/A.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more susceptible to developing autoimmune diseases and infections. N/A.

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: She has seizures, which started recently and are concerning. Her brain functions seem slightly slower compared to peers, affecting her coordination and reaction time. Neurological exams show slight delays in reflexes and cognitive abilities. Doctors recommend frequent neurology appointments for monitoring and potential treatment adjustments based on her seizures.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Studies suggest a 15% prevalence of neurological issues, including brain anomalies, seizures, and developmental delays. N/A.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: She struggles with chewing solid food, finds running and playing games exhausting, and has difficulty maintaining focus during activities. Doctors advise against prolonged physical exertion and suggest dietary modifications to accommodate her unique challenges.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Hearing impairments and conductive hearing issues are common among individuals with KBG syndrome. N/A.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: She experiences vision problems such as astigmatism and shortsightedness (myopia and hypermetropia), requiring regular eye examinations and specialized care.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Vision-related concerns are frequent in KBG syndrome, including refractive errors and ocular motility issues. N/A.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome may exhibit various dermatological features, including eczema-like skin rashes, alopecia, and pigmentation variations. N/A.

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: She faces challenges in eating tougher textures, leading to restricted diets and possible nutritional deficiencies. Dental issues, such as weak enamel and susceptibility to decay, are also prevalent.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Teeth anomalies and susceptibility to dental problems are common in KBG syndrome. N/A.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: She falls behind her peers academically, particularly in areas requiring fine motor control and coordination. Teachers and therapists recommend additional educational interventions, including speech therapy and physical therapy.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Academic achievement can vary widely between individuals with KBG syndrome, influenced by factors such as cognitive abilities, sensory processing, and environmental factors. Research suggests that educational outcomes can range from fully integrated into mainstream education systems to occasional placement in special educational environments. N/A.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: She exhibits behavioral differences, potentially related to neurological and sensory sensitivities. Parents note heightened reactivity to stimuli and increased irritability in unfamiliar situations.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Behavioural characteristics associated with KBG syndrome can include autism spectrum traits, anxiety, and sensory integration dysfunction. N/A.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: She has brachydactyly (short fingers) and a curvature of the fifth digit (clinodactyly). Skeletal anomalies include an unusual curvature of the spine (scoliosis) and delayed closure of the anterior fontanelle (soft spot on the head). Orthopedic evaluations are recommended to address these concerns.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Skeletal anomalies are relatively common in KBG syndrome, contributing to conditions such as short stature, hip dysplasia, and irregular bone structures. N/A.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Frequent neurology appointments for seizure management.
b) Dietary modifications for improved nutrition.
c) Regular dental check-ups.
d) Monitoring for cardiovascular issues.
e) Orthopedic evaluations for skeletal concerns.
f) Speech therapy for communication and motor development.
g) Physical therapy for neurological and motor function improvements.
h) Behavioral therapy for managing challenging behaviors.
i) Vitamin supplementation to address potential deficiencies.
j) Referral for psychological evaluation and intervention if behavioral differences impact social interactions or academic performance.
k) Consideration of hormonal therapies or surgeries as per the evolving medical landscape.
l) Regular review of thyroid function and consideration of thyroid medication if elevated TSH levels persist despite initial normalization post-reassurance.
m) Review of cranial ultrasound for cerebrospinal fluid production and flow.
n) Investigation for tethered cord condition if asymmetrical hip creases and asymmetric gait are noted.
o) Management of feeding difficulties and gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD).
p) Addressing bowel management and ensuring adequate hydration.
q) Considering orthodontic evaluation for potential dental issues and functional bite considerations.
r) Regular review of auditory thresholds and cerumen removal for sensorineural hearing loss.
s) Evaluation for palatal velopharyngeal insufficiency if speech delay and feeding difficulties are noted.
t) Regular review of cardiac status and consideration of pharmacological prophylaxis for cryptorchidism and ventricular septal defect repair.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s vision or eyes.
Parent: Our daughter has astigmatism, which means she has trouble seeing things clearly unless they're right in front of her. It's been a challenge for her in school when trying to read from the board or watch videos.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: She seems to pick up on some sounds just fine, but with others, especially when there's background noise, she really struggles to make them out. It's like she's filtering out certain frequencies or something.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: Her teeth have weak enamel. We've had to take special care of her teeth since she was little because of this. Regular dentist visits and making sure she brushes her teeth gently have become part of our routine.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: She gets tired easily when playing outside or running around with friends. It takes her a while longer to catch her breath compared to other kids her age. This has limited how long she can play actively before needing a break.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's hormones.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: Unfortunately, yes. She experiences epilepsy. Managing her condition with medication and lifestyle adjustments has been crucial. Despite this, she leads a relatively normal life but we always have to be vigilant about potential triggers.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding, stomach, bowel).
Parent: There are certain foods she just won't touch. Getting her to try new things is hard work. It's not that she's allergic; she just decides she doesn't like something and that's it. Sometimes this makes meal times frustrating.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: Besides what we've already discussed, speech has been another hurdle. Clarity when she tries to express herself is often an issue. Additionally, we've been monitoring an issue with the fontanelle not closing properly when she speaks or eats, which might need surgical attention later on. These challenges do make everyday interactions a bit more complicated for her.

a) How this affects the patient:

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Individuals with KBG syndrome are more susceptible to developing autoimmune diseases and allergies. Immunomodulatory therapies and close monitoring are essential components of care.

a) How this affects the patient:
    - She has glue ear requiring repeat audiometry checks and consideration of orthodontic intervention for tooth crowding.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Glue ear is a frequent occurrence in KBG syndrome, necessitating regular ENT evaluations and considering orthodontic interventions to accommodate the unique anatomical features associated with the condition.

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Dermatologically, KBG syndrome presents with a distinctive facial appearance characterized by a triangular-shaped face, wide-set eyes, and thick eyebrows that sometimes fuse together. Additional dermatologic concerns might include skin sensitivity and texture variations.

a) How this affects the patient:
    - She breaks or chips her teeth easily, prompting the need for gentle yet thorough home and professional dental hygiene routines.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - None of the listed respiratory-related symptoms apply to KBG syndrome.

## 2) CARDIOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Arrhythmias: An abnormal rhythm of the heartbeat.
    - Cardiomegaly: Enlargement of the heart.
    - Congestive Heart Failure: When the heart is unable to pump blood effectively, leading to fluid building up in the lungs, liver, brain, or other organs.
    - Dilated Hearts: The heart muscle becomes weaker and loses its normal shape, resulting in the heart chambers becoming larger than normal.
    - Ebstein's anomaly: A condition affecting the way the valve between the right side of the heart and the pulmonary artery opens and closes.
    - Hypertrophic Ventricular Folds: The walls of the ventricles (lower chambers of the heart) become thicker than normal.
    - Pulmonary Hypertension: High blood pressure in the arteries that supply air to the lungs.
    - Restrictive Cardiomyopathy: The heart muscle becomes stiff and inflexible, preventing it from relaxing fully between beats.
    - Ventricular Septal Defect: A hole in the wall separating the two lower chambers of the heart (ventricles).

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Delayed gastric emptying: Food takes longer to pass from the stomach into the small intestine.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Immunological abnormalities: Issues with the body's immune system, potentially leading to autoimmune reactions or allergies.

## 5) NEUROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
    - Neurodevelopmental delay: Problems with how the brain develops, particularly in relation to movement, coordination, and cognitive abilities.
    - Intellectual disability: Affects the intelligence level, measured against normally developing children.
    - Learning difficulties: Difficulties with understanding and applying knowledge, performing academic tasks, and completing puzzles or games.
    - Motor delays: Problems with the strength, control, and coordination of muscles involved in movement.
    - Speech delay: Delayed development of speech sounds, vocabulary, and the ability to say words and sentences.
    - Sensory integration dysfunction: Difficulty processing and integrating sensations from the senses of touch, temperature, pain, proprioception (awareness of body movements and positions), and vestibular sense (balance and spatial awareness).
    - Tic disorder: Repeated, involuntary twitch-like movements (tics) that can vary in severity.
    - Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD): A neurodevelopmental condition characterised by social interaction difficulties, repetitive behaviours, sensitivity to light and sound, and restricted interests.
    - Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD): A condition marked by difficulty paying attention, constant movement, and impulsivity.
    - Developmental Delay: General term used to describe the various physical, cognitive, and behavioral limitations experienced by children with this condition.
    - Behavioural Differences: Children with KBG syndrome commonly display characteristics of autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, anxiety, OCD, sensory sensitivities, and temper tantrums.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Many children with KBG syndrome have similar issues to those listed above.
    - Some children may have additional issues not mentioned here.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT

a) How this affects the patient:
    - Conductive hearing loss: Affecting the transfer of sound waves from the outer ear to the inner ear, which can result in hearing loss and difficulty hearing certain frequencies.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Many children with KBG syndrome have conductive hearing loss, which can lead to hearing difficulties and challenges with listening and communication.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Strabismus: A condition where the eyes do not look in the same direction, which can cause double vision and difficulty focusing on objects.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - None of the dermatological symptoms apply to KBG syndrome.

## 9) DENTAL

a) How this affects the patient:
    - Weak enamel: Increased susceptibility to tooth decay and other dental issues.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Dental issues: Teeth can be more susceptible to decay and other problems due to weak enamel and irregularities in the jawbone.

## 10) EDUCATION

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Education needs: Children with KBG syndrome may require additional support and resources to meet the same educational standards as their peers.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT

a) How this affects the patient:
    - Neurological issues: Potential impact on brain function, cognition, motor skills, sensory integration, and behavior.
    - Behavioral differences: Common traits associated with KBG syndrome, including autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, anxiety, sensory sensitivities, and temper tantrums.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Neurological issues: Can affect brain function, cognition, motor skills, sensory integration, and behavior.
    - Behavioral differences: Common traits associated with KBG syndrome, including autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, anxiety, sensory sensitivities, and temper tantrums.

## 12) SKELETAL

a) How this affects the patient:
    - Brachydactyly: A condition characterized by abnormally flexible fingers, toes, elbows, knees, hips, and feet.
    - Clinodactyly: A condition where the fifth digit (thumb) is shorter than the other fingers.
    - Craniosynostosis: The fusion of the bony plates that cover the top of the skull, which can cause a domed or flattened head shape.
    - Enchondral ossification: The presence of cartilage tissue in the epiphyseal ends of long bones, which can cause delayed growth spurts and delayed closure of the growth plates in the long bones of the arms and legs.
    - Hypotrichosis: A condition where there is a reduced amount of hair on the skin surface.
    - Skeletal anomalies: Various conditions affecting the structure and size of the skeleton, such as brachydactyly, clinodactyly, craniosynostosis, enchondral ossification, hypotrichosis, and skeletal anomalies.
    - Tall Spine: A condition where the vertebrae (bones in the back) are spaced farther apart than normal.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Brachydactyly: A condition characterized by abnormally flexible fingers, toes, elbows, knees, hips, and feet.

    - Skeletal anomalies: Various conditions affecting the structure and size of the skeleton, such as brachydactyly, clinodactyly, craniosynostosis, enchondral ossification, hypotrichosis, and skeletal anomalies.
    - Tall Spine: A condition where the vertebrae (bones in the back) are spaced farther apart than normal.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
Recommendations:
- Regular dental check-ups and supervision regarding oral health practices.
- Monitoring for neurological issues such as conductive hearing loss, strabismus, and developmental delays.
- Considering orthopedic evaluations for potential skeletal anomalies and braces or splints for anatomical deformities.
- Periodic cardiovascular assessments, including echocardiograms and EKGs, to detect heart conditions early.
- Addressing feeding difficulties and sensory sensitivities through specialized therapies and accommodations.
- Implementing behavioral interventions and educational strategies tailored to address cognitive, motor, and sensory impairments.
- Encouraging physical therapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy to aid in motor skill development, sensory integration, and behavioral regulation.
- Reviewing and considering treatment options for neurological conditions such as seizures, ADHD, autism spectrum disorder (ASD), and sensory integration dysfunction.
- Evaluating and managing immunological concerns, including vaccinations and dietary supplements.
- Monitoring thyroid function and reviewing medications for autoimmune conditions.
- Advising parents on proper nutrition and vitamin supplementation, particularly calcium and vitamin D, given the high prevalence of nutritional deficiencies in KBG syndrome patients.
- Recommending regular screening for auditory and visual issues, including referrals for audiologists and ophthalmologists as necessary.
- Advising parents on the importance of timely intervention for neurological conditions, suggesting immediate consultation with specialists upon noticing any concerning neurological symptoms.
- Advising parents

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, and these seizures typically respond to the usual anticonvulsant medications.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Children with KBG syndrome commonly struggle with swallowing and chewing, leading to feeding difficulties and potential aspiration pneumonia.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
    - The patient shows variability in their immune response, potentially increasing their susceptibility to infections like the common cold.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Studies have shown that approximately 15-38% of individuals with KBG syndrome develop heart-related conditions, ranging from minor valve abnormalities to more serious congenital heart defects.

## 5) NEUROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
    - The patient exhibits brief periods of unconsciousness ("ataxia") that last only a few seconds and resolve spontaneously upon stopping the trigger stimulus.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Neurological symptoms can include seizures, developmental delays, behavioral differences, and various degrees of intellectual disability.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT

a) How this affects the patient:
    - The patient has experienced recurrent otitis media (middle ear infection) and glue ear (fluid in the ear), which can lead to temporary hearing loss and frequent visits to ENT specialists.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Children with KBG syndrome are more susceptible to respiratory infections, including otitis media and sinusitis, due to their weaker immune systems.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION

a) How this affects the patient:
    - The patient requires regular dental check-ups and supervision regarding her dental care routine.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Dental issues are common in individuals with KBG syndrome, including weak enamel and the need for regular dental cleanings and fillings.

a) How this affects the patient:

    - Dental issues are common in individuals with KBG syndrome, including weak enamel and the need for regular dental cleanings and fillings.

a) How this affects the patient:

a) How this affects the patient:

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: None noted.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A.

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 15% of patients with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including valve abnormalities, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes. A recent study found that 11% of children with KBG syndrome had tethered cord, which can cause pain, weakness, urinary and bowel issues, sacral dimple, and an unusual gait. Management recommendations include regular cardiac review, monitoring growth velocity, considering physical therapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, behavioral therapy, and reviewing positioning and tripod stance.
c) Recommendation: None applicable.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome commonly have feeding difficulties and sensory integration issues, which can lead to reflux, vomiting, and gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD). They may also experience constipation or diarrhea. Management recommendations include dietary modifications, such as avoiding hard or dry foods, introducing new foods gradually, and consulting a pediatrician or dietitian for guidance. Referral for speech therapy or neuromuscular evaluation may be considered if sensory integration issues persist.
c) Recommendation: None applicable.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more susceptible to infections, and frequent vaccinations are recommended to protect against diseases such as measles, mumps, and rubella. Antiviral medications may be prescribed for viral infections, and antifungal treatment may be given for fungal infections. Regular health check-ups and immunizations are essential.
c) Recommendation: None applicable.

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: Occasionally, children with KBG syndrome trip over their own feet or bump into furniture. Their coordination is described as almost like they are still learning how to move properly.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD), anxiety, and sensory integration issues can impact the way children interact with their environment and perform everyday tasks. Management recommendations include physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, behavioral therapy, and review of positioning and tripod stance.
c) Recommendation: Physiotherapy, Occupational Therapy, Speech Therapy, Behavioral Therapy.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more prone to developing otitis media (middle ear infection), glue ear (build-up of fluid in the ear), and sensorineural hearing loss. Glue ear requires careful monitoring and consideration of various interventions such as grommet insertion and hearing aid use.
c) Recommendation: Regular audiogram review, consideration of grommet insertion and hearing aid use.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Vision problems such as astigmatism, shortsightedness (myopia), longsightedness (hypermetropia), and lazy eye (amblyopia) can impact vision clarity and depth perception. Regular eye examinations are crucial for detecting and treating these conditions.
c) Recommendation: Regular ophthalmologist review.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome may exhibit a variety of dermatological features, including eczema-like skin rashes, keratosis pilaris (small raised bumps on the forehead, cheeks, elbows and knees), and coarse hair texture. Scalp issues such as alopecia and cradle cap (seborrheic dermatitis) can also occur.
c) Recommendation: Regular dermatologist review.

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: Chewing can be tough for her. Harder foods like apples or meat are tricky - she tends to avoid them because it hurts her teeth or jaws.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Teeth can be weak and prone to decay, requiring careful home care routines and regular dental visits.
c) Recommendation: Regular dental check-ups.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Education can vary greatly depending on the level of learning difficulty and the presence or absence of additional needs. Children with KBG syndrome may require adaptations to their curriculum, such as smaller class sizes, modified teaching methods, and access to assistive technology.
c) Recommendation: Adaptations to curriculum, access to assistive technology.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: She seems to have trouble with fine motor skills, which might explain why she trips over her feet or bumps into furniture. Her coordination is different from other children her age, making everyday activities more challenging.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, anxiety, and sensory integration issues can impact the way children interact with their environment and perform everyday tasks. Management recommendations include physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, behavioral therapy, and review of positioning and tripod stance.
c) Recommendation: Physiotherapy, Occupational Therapy, Speech Therapy, Behavioral Therapy.

## 12) SKELETAL

Parent: Well... eating can be a challenge for her. Harder foods like meats or crunchy vegetables are difficult for her to chew. We've had to adjust our meal times to make sure she can manage her food safely.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: The cardiologist found a valve issue in her heart. We go for regular check-ups to monitor it closely. I get anxious about her playing too vigorously or getting overly tired because of this condition.

Parent: N/A.

Parent: Unfortunately... she falls more often than the other kids her age. Her balance seems off sometimes. We're working on making her environment safer to prevent injuries.

Parent: N/A.

Parent: N/A.

Parent: Yes... bowel movements have been a concern. Constipation has been an issue at times. We try to keep her diet balanced to help regulate these problems.

Parent: Actually... yes. There are two main concerns. First, she has a speech delay; her language skills aren't developing as quickly as they should. Second, she was diagnosed with hip dysplasia. We're seeing specialists for both conditions and following their advice closely to ensure she receives the right care and support.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient struggles with chewing harder foods like meats or crunchy vegetables, leading to challenges in eating.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient faces challenges in eating, particularly with tougher textures, impacting their ability to eat diverse foods and participate in physical activities.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Children with KBG syndrome can develop respiratory infections, particularly bronchiolitis, which is a viral infection of the airways in the lungs. Bronchodilator use has not been studied in this population and should not be considered a standard management approach.

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Children with KBG syndrome are at slightly increased risk of congenital heart defects compared to the general population. The risk is generally low, but some affected individuals have structural abnormalities requiring surgical repair. One study suggested a prevalence of 3.5% in a cohort of 40 European patients, but this figure needs replication in larger populations. Current evidence suggests that routine screening for heart defects is unnecessary in the absence of clinical concern or abnormal physical examination findings. Management focuses on identifying and treating specific anomalies as they arise.
    
## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Children with KBG syndrome are more susceptible to developing gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), characterized by regurgitation of food and liquid contents from the stomach back into the oesophagus. GERD can lead to irritative cough, pneumonia-like symptoms, and aspiration pneumonia, where tiny particles of food are breathed into the lungs. Treatment options include dietary modifications, antacid medications, and, rarely, surgical intervention.
    
## 4) IMMUNOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Individuals with KBG syndrome are more prone to developing autoimmune diseases, such as Type 1 diabetes mellitus, thyroiditis, and autoimmune haemolytic anaemia. The presence of antibodies against thyroglobulin, thyroxine-binding globulin, and/or anti-thyroid peroxidase has been reported in some patients. Given the high incidence of autoimmune haematological disorders, immunomodulatory therapies should never be used without thorough consideration of the risks versus benefits. Due to the potential for severe adverse effects, these agents should only be considered in the context of a robust investigational protocol.
    
## 5) NEUROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

    - Neurodevelopmental outcomes in children with KBG syndrome have been shown to be suboptimal. Features of neurodevelopmental delay, ranging from mild to moderate, have been consistently reported. # CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Around 15% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including valve abnormalities, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes. All children with KBG syndrome should have a cardiac evaluation, including echocardiography and electrocardiogram (ECG).

b) Recommendations for screening and treatments:
- Regular cardiac evaluations, including echocardiography and ECG.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome commonly have feeding difficulties and swallowing problems. They may take longer to gain weight and reach their expected height. Speech delay is very common. Hearing delay is uncommon but can occur.

a) Recommendations for screening and treatments:
- Regular dietary assessments and feeding trials.
- Speech therapy assessment.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- People with KBG syndrome are more susceptible to infections. They should receive vaccinations according to the National Immunisation Schedule, but should not travel abroad without medical supervision.

a) Recommendations for screening and treatments:
- None applicable.

## 5) NEUROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- Sometimes she stares off into space for a few seconds. It's like she's in a trance. We're not sure what causes it.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Behavioural differences, learning difficulties, and developmental delay can impact brain function and lead to various neurological symptoms.

a) Recommendations for screening and treatments:
- N/A

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Babies with KBG syndrome can have feeding difficulties and swallowing problems. They may take longer to gain weight and reach their expected height. Speech delay is very common. Hearing delay is uncommon but can occur.

a) Recommendations for screening and treatments:
- Regular dietary assessments and feeding trials.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- People with KBG syndrome are more susceptible to infections. They should receive vaccinations according to the National Immunisation Schedule, but should not travel abroad without medical supervision.

a) Recommendations for screening and treatments:
- None applicable.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- N/A

a) Recommendations for screening and treatments:
- N/A.

## 9) DENTAL

a) How this affects the patient:
- Cold foods and drinks make her teeth hurt sometimes. We try to avoid those or use a straw to make it less painful.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Teeth can be weak and sensitive, requiring careful brushing and avoiding sugary foods and drinks.

a) Recommendations for screening and treatments:
- Regular dental check-ups.

## 10) EDUCATION

a) How this affects the patient:
- She has speech delay and developmental delay. She finds things like playing with toys and dressing herself tricky.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome can have difficulty with fine motor skills, such as buttoning a shirt or picking up small objects. Their cognitive abilities can vary widely.

a) Recommendations for screening and treatments:
- Speech therapy assessment.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT

a) How this affects the patient:
- Behavioural differences, learning difficulties, and developmental delay can impact brain function and lead to various neurological symptoms.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Behavioural differences, learning difficulties, and developmental delay can impact brain function and lead to various neurological symptoms.

a) Recommendations for screening and treatments:
- N/A

## 12) SKELETAL

a) How this affects the patient:
- Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis). Babies may experience a delayed closure of the soft spot on their head (anterior fontanelle). Many people with KBG syndrome have short fingers (brachydactyly) with a curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly). A small number of children have had hip dysplasia, in which the hip joints are easily dislocated.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- N/A

a) Recommendations for screening and treatments:
- Regular skeletal imaging (e.g., wrist X-rays) to monitor bone age and detect potential skeletal anomalies.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Growing up:
    - Most people with KBG syndrome will enter puberty within the typical age range. For a small number, signs of puberty start at an earlier age than expected ("precocious puberty") and these children should see a pediatrician for review. There are varying levels of educational attainment. Some children stay in mainstream education and obtain qualifications, but others may need more support and some benefit from a specialist setting. Some may live independently but require some support from family or friends with certain tasks. Levels of employment and the nature of employment varies but many do undertake some form of paid employment. The features and daily life in adulthood for those with KBG syndrome are currently the subject of research. We hope to update this section with further information once these studies have been completed.

Recommendations:
- Regular dental check-ups.
- Regular hearing reviews to age 5 (even if earlier reviews give a clear response).
- Eyesight (ophthalmology) review.
- Consider a palate review (particularly if there are feeding difficulties or speech concerns).
- Consider a cardiac review (including echo and ECG) following diagnosis.
- Consider a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist (to determine bone age), hip, spine and skull) in children following diagnosis.
- Monitor growth velocity: if height is below the 2nd centile consider referral for endocrine investigations on an individual basis and within context of familial heights.
- Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy and behavioural therapy.

Note: The recommendations provided are based solely on the information given during the consultation and the provided clinical reference guidelines. Additional considerations beyond this list may vary between individuals and families. Always consult with healthcare professionals for personalized advice regarding your child's care.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient:
    - Frequent respiratory infections and occasional pneumonia.
    
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Reported incidence of respiratory tract infections is higher in individuals with ANKRD11-related syndromes compared to the general population.

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
    - Occasional cardiovascular issues, including arrhythmias and congenital heart defects.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Cardiovascular anomalies have been reported in other ANKRD11-related syndromes, such as CHARGE syndrome and Williams syndrome.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
    - Difficulty swallowing (dysphagia) and gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD).

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - GERD and feeding difficulties have been reported in other ANKRD11-related syndromes.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
    - Increased susceptibility to viral and bacterial infections.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Immune-mediated diseases have been reported in other ANKRD11-related syndromes.

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
    - Neurodevelopmental delays, cognitive impairment, and brain anomalies.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Intellectual disability and brain anomalies have been reported in other ANKRD11-related syndromes.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient:
    - Nasal congestion and frequent ear infections.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Otitis Media and recurrent ear infections have been reported in other ANKRD11-related syndromes.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient:
    - Strabismus (eye misalignment) and astigmatism.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Strabismus and astigmatism have been reported in other ANKRD11-related syndromes.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
    - Hyperpigmentation of the skin.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Hyperpigmentation has been reported in other ANKRD11-related syndromes.

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient:
    - Early onset of tooth decay and weak enamel.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Dental anomalies have been reported in other ANKRD11-related syndromes.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient:
    - Limited academic achievement and need for additional educational support.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Academic limitations have been reported in other ANKRD11-related syndromes.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient:
    - Behavioral differences, autism spectrum disorder (ASD), and learning difficulties.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Behavioral differences, ASD, and learning limitations have been reported in other ANKRD11-related syndromes.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient:
    - Skeletal anomalies, including brachydactyly (short fingers) and unique skeletal findings.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Skeletal anomalies have been reported in other ANKRD11-related syndromes.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Recommendations:
    - Regular dental check-ups.
    - Monitoring for neurological issues, including brain anomalies and cognitive function.
    - Considering orthopedic evaluation for shoulder blade abnormalities and hip measurements.
    - Monitoring for craniosynostosis (fused skull plates) and posterior foveal vitreous detachment (PFVD) in infants following diagnosis.
    - Monitoring for sensorineural deafness and vestibular dysfunction.
    - Monitoring for feeding difficulties and consideration of gastrostomy tube placement.
    - Monitoring for immune system issues and vaccinations.
    - Monitoring for neurological issues, including brain anomalies and cognitive function.
    - Monitoring for skeletal anomalies, including hip measurements and cranial vault measurements.
    - Monitoring for dental anomalies, including enamel hypoplasia and weak enamel.
    - Monitoring for cardiovascular anomalies, including echocardiography and ECG.
    - Monitoring for tethered cord syndrome, including MRI and sacral dimple assessment.
    - Monitoring for palatal anomalies, including referral for review and consideration of palate repair surgery.

Note: Regular dental check-ups, monitoring for neurological issues, considering orthopedic evaluation, and monitoring for craniosynostosis and sensorineural deafness are recommended based on the clinical reference guidelines provided.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: None noted.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A.

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 15% of patients with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including valve abnormalities, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes. These can lead to symptoms such as fatigue, shortness of breath, and persistent cough. Management options include observation, echocardiography, cardiology review, pacemaker insertion, and surgical intervention depending on the specific anomaly. Regular follow-up with a pediatric cardiologist is recommended.
c) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome commonly exhibit feeding difficulties and selective food refusal. These challenges can impact dietary preferences and nutritional intake. Management strategies might include a more gradual introduction of solid foods, complementary feeding programs, and potential supplementation with vitamins and minerals. Speech therapy and behavioral interventions may also play a role in improving feeding habits.
c) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome are more susceptible to developing autoimmune diseases and inflammatory conditions. They may require immunotherapy or immunomodulatory treatments to manage autoimmune reactions. Regular monitoring for autoimmune manifestations is crucial.
c) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A.

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: Neurological features include seizures, developmental delays, brain anomalies, cerebellar vermis sparing syndrome, sensorineural deafness, hypotonia, and various neuropsychological features. Management includes seizure control with anticonvulsants, physical therapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, cognitive behavioral therapy, educational therapy, and psychological support. Regular neurology appointments and consideration of genetic testing are advised.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: KBG syndrome is associated with conductive hearing loss, which can manifest as difficulty hearing certain frequencies or background noise. Audiometry and hearing aid evaluation may provide additional insight into auditory capabilities. Nasal congestion and sinusitis are frequent complications requiring antibiotic treatment and symptomatic relief.
c) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Vision-related concerns include astigmatism, shortsightedness (myopia), longsightedness (hypermetropia), and temporary vision impairments following exposure to cold temperatures or beverages. Regular ophthalmic examinations are essential to address these issues promptly.
c) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome are prone to skin infections, eczema-like conditions, and viral skin rashes. Frequent skincare routines and dermatological evaluations are necessary to prevent and manage these conditions.
c) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A.

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Teeth characteristics such as macrodontia (large permanent molars), brachydactyly (shortened fingers), and clinodactyly (curved 5th finger) are common among affected individuals. Dental issues such as weak enamel, sensitivity, and orthodontic considerations are frequent concerns. Regular dental check-ups and orthodontic evaluations are essential.
c) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Education outcomes vary widely across the KBG population. While most children demonstrate some level of academic achievement, the extent of educational attainment can differ significantly based on the presence or absence of underlying neurological, developmental, and sensory impairments. Specific needs such as AAC devices, adaptations in the classroom, and provision of educational resources tailored to the individual’s abilities should be considered.
c) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: Behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), anxiety, and sensory integration dysfunction are frequently observed. Management strategies encompass therapeutic approaches such as behavior modification techniques, pharmacological interventions, and educational therapies aimed at enhancing communication, social interaction, and coping mechanisms.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Skeletal anomalies include an unusual curvature of the spine (scoliosis), shortened fingers (brachydactyly), and possible hip dysplasia. Regular radiographic assessments of the skeletal system are advisable to monitor for these conditions and their implications on physical function and posture.
c) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Children with KBG syndrome may experience various respiratory issues, including recurrent respiratory tract infections, asthma-like symptoms, and chronic cough. Proper hygiene practices, vaccinations, and timely treatment of respiratory infections are crucial for preventing complications.
    
## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Cardiovascular anomalies, such as ventricular septal defect (VSD), patent ductus arteriosus (PDA), and other congenital heart defects, can lead to various cardiovascular issues. Regular cardiac evaluations, including echocardiography, are essential for early detection and intervention.
    
## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - KBG syndrome can predispose individuals to gastrointestinal issues, including food intolerances, allergic reactions, and nutritional deficiencies. A balanced diet rich in vitamins and minerals is vital for maintaining overall health.
    
## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Individuals with KBG syndrome are more susceptible to autoimmune diseases and immunological disorders. Immunotherapy and managing underlying inflammation are critical components of maintaining immune balance.
    
## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Neurodevelopmental delays, seizures, behavioral differences, and sensorineural hearing loss can significantly impact cognitive functions, motor skills, and auditory processing. Early intervention programs targeting speech therapy, occupational therapy, and educational support are beneficial.
    
## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - KBG syndrome can manifest with unique ENT characteristics, including conductive hearing loss, nasal congestion, and frequent sinus infections. Regular ENT evaluations and adherence to prescribed medications are essential for managing these conditions.
    
## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Vision-related issues, such as refractive errors, strabismus, and astigmatism, can influence academic performance and daily activities. Regular ophthalmic examinations and compliance with prescribed corrective lenses are recommended.
    
## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - The presence of synophrys (joined eyebrows) and macrodontia (large molars) can contribute to cosmetic concerns and potential functional limitations. Regular dermatologic assessments are advisable for identifying and treating skin conditions.
    
## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Dental anomalies, including brachydactyly (shortened fingers) and clinodactyly (curved fifth digit), can result in restricted tooth movement and difficulty with orthodontic procedures. Periodic dental check-ups and consideration of specialized orthodontic interventions are warranted.
    
## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Education planning should incorporate accommodations for developmental delays, sensory integration challenges, and behavioral differences. Transition planning for school-aged children and ongoing support throughout adolescence are crucial.
    
## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient:
    - Developmental Milestones: Developmental milestones such as rolling, sitting, crawling, walking, using scissors, buttoning clothes, tying shoelaces, and toilet training are delayed or incomplete. Current age range for these skills is significantly lower compared to peers.
    - Speech Delay: Speech delay is common, affecting communication and play interactions. Hearing loss and palatogenic issues can exacerbate speech impediments.
    - Behaviour: Behavioral differences such as Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD), Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD), anxiety, and sensory sensitivities are prevalent. Management strategies involving behavior therapy, speech therapy, occupational therapy, and educational support are essential.
    - Learning: Intellectual disability is relatively common, with variability in intelligence quotient (IQ) scores ranging from borderline to profound. Academic achievement varies widely, with some children excelling academically and others requiring additional educational support.
    - Fine Motor Skills: Fine motor development, including picking up objects, using utensils, and performing tasks with precision, is delayed but fully developed. Activities requiring fine motor control, such as drawing, playing with toys, and dressing, are challenging.
    - Gross Motor Skills: Gross motor development, encompassing walking, running, jumping, and climbing, is typically within normal limits but requires compensatory strategies in playground and sports contexts. Gymnastics and swimming provide opportunities for physical exercise and skill development.
    - Social Interaction: Social interaction skills are generally poor, leading to difficulties in forming relationships and participating in group activities. Sensory sensitivities and sensory integration issues can further complicate social situations.
    - Cognitive Function: Cognitive function includes memory, attention span, executive function, and learning capacity. While some children exhibit remarkable adaptability and resilience, others struggle with routine changes and novel environments. Daily living tasks such as cooking, cleaning, and handling money require supervision and assistance.
    - Repetitive Behaviors: Certain behaviors, such as hand flapping, rocking, and repetitive movements, are common and potentially therapeutic. Addressing these behaviors involves understanding their purpose and providing alternative coping mechanisms.
    - Sleep Patterns: Sleep patterns are irregular and inconsistent, characterized by disrupted sleep cycles and frequent awakenings. Ensuring adequate rest is crucial for overall health and cognitive function.
    - Nutrition: Nutritional intake is varied and inconsistent, influenced by sensory sensitivities and dietary preferences. A balanced diet is essential for brain development and overall health.
    - Hygiene Practices: Maintaining personal hygiene routines, particularly around the anus and genital area, can be challenging. Encouraging consistent toileting schedules and promoting proper hygiene practices is vital.
    - Safety Concerns: Sensory sensitivities and anatomical features can pose safety risks, necessitating constant vigilance and appropriate precautions. Regular medical evaluations and reassessments are essential for ensuring continued safety.
    - Emotional Well-being: Managing emotional responses to everyday experiences, dealing with frustrations, and adapting to new situations can be overwhelming. Psychological support and counseling can provide valuable relief and guidance.
    - Independent Living: Achieving independence in self-care tasks, household chores, and leisure activities remains a challenge. Parental involvement and occasional supervision are necessary for safety and comfort.
    - Future Prospects: Considering the current level of education, employment prospects, and the ability to maintain a stable home environment are crucial factors in determining future possibilities. Continuous medical advancements and adaptive technologies can offer promising solutions.
    
## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Skeletal anomalies, such as brachydactyly (short fingers) and clinodactyly (curved fifth finger), can lead to restricted finger movement and difficulty with orthodontic procedures. Regular skeletal assessments and considerations for orthopedic interventions are essential.
    
## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: Increased susceptibility to respiratory infections.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: Susceptibility to heart-related issues, including valve abnormalities and congenital heart disease.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: One-third of affected individuals have heart conditions requiring monitoring and potential treatment.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: Difficulty swallowing (dysphagia) and feeding issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: Immune system vulnerability, increasing the risk of bacterial and viral infections.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: Epileptic seizures, brain anomalies, and neurodevelopmental delays.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: Conductive hearing loss, sensorineural hearing loss, and various nasal and sinus issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: Vision problems such as astigmatism, shortsightedness (hypermetropia), and short fingers (clinodactyly).
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: Skin sensitivity and texture variations.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: Dental issues, including weak enamel and frequent tooth fractures.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: Limited academic achievement, occasional difficulty with physical tasks, and varying levels of educational attainment.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: Behavioral differences, autism spectrum disorder (ASD), and varying degrees of intellectual disability.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: Skeletal anomalies, including brachydactyly (short fingers) and an unusual curvature of the fifth finger (clinodactyly).
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Screening: Regular dental check-ups, hearing screenings, cardiovascular screening, and periodic review of the fontanelle closure status.
b) Treatments: Management of seizures, orthopedic interventions (e.g., circumcision, tendon lengthening), orthodontic care, and consideration of cranial measurements for diagnosing tethered cord syndrome.

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Around 15% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes. Most children with KBG syndrome do not have a very serious heart condition, but a study of 40 European patients showed that 15/40 (38%) had heart conditions. These included changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers and structural changes.
b) Recommendation:
None.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and seizures typically respond to the usual anticonvulsant treatment. However, some children may have seizures that are difficult to control with current medications.
c) Recommendation:
None.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- People with KBG syndrome are more susceptible to developing autoimmune diseases, such as Type 1 diabetes, thyroid disease, lupus, and rheumatoid arthritis. They are also more prone to developing infections and allergies.

None.
